result.summary:
Applied the fix exactly as ISSUE-FIXER specified in test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs, describe 'configurable memory limit (REQ-156)', the AC-1 test (was lines 625-658). Removed: both :timer.tc/1 wrappers (small_elapsed_us/large_elapsed_us), the small_elapsed_ms/large_elapsed_ms derived-value computation, and the `assert small_elapsed_ms < large_elapsed_ms, ...` flaky wall-clock comparison entirely. Unchanged (verified via git diff, byte-identical): `assert {:error, :memory_limit_exceeded} = small_result` and `assert {:ok, %{manifest_hash: _}} = large_result` -- the deterministic outcome pair that alone satisfies AC-1/T1's load-bearing-limit property per REQ-156.md T1's own accepted 'outcome differs' alternative to a pure timing comparison. Renamed the test from 'AC-1: a smaller configured max_heap_words halts sooner than a larger one on the same allocating script' to 'AC-1: a smaller configured max_heap_words halts the allocating script while a materially larger one lets the same script complete', and appended a new comment paragraph above the test (citing ISS-0469 and ISS-0446 as the two prior flakes at this file:line) explaining the removal is deletion-of-redundancy, not a coverage cut. No other lines in the file were touched (confirmed by git diff scope: only lines 625-658 changed).

Verification performed in this environment (Elixir 1.20.3-otp-29, Erlang/OTP 29, via asdf shims):
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean, zero output, both before and after the edit (also re-verified against a `git stash` of the change to confirm no pre-existing warning regression).
- `mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs --seed <N>` run 5 times with distinct seeds (11, 22, 33, 44, 55): all green, 'Finished in ~7.3s' each run, no failures. A separate warning ('the following clause will never match', at line 466 in an unrelated pre-existing test, 'AC-4 regression guard') appears identically on the unmodified file (confirmed via git stash) and under plain `mix test` -- pre-existing, unrelated to this change, and not raised by `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` on the application build.
- As ISSUE-FIXER's own next_action anticipated: since ISS-0469 was a wall-clock CI-scheduler-contention flake, local reruns were already reliably green before this fix too -- the real proof of the fix is structural (grep confirms zero remaining references to small_elapsed_ms/large_elapsed_ms/small_elapsed_us/large_elapsed_us anywhere in the file, and the test body now contains no :timer.tc call at all), not a local repro of the flake.
- grep -n 'small_elapsed\|large_elapsed' test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs: only match is the new explanatory comment's own prose (mentioning the removed identifiers by name for context), not code.

AC-1 coverage preserved, not weakened: the git diff shows the two outcome-assertion lines are untouched (same text, same position relative to the two calls), which is the entire substance the spec (REQ-156.md T1) requires for AC-1. No production code (lib/letflow/) or migrations touched -- test-only change, no tenant-data path, so per orchestrator guidance this routes directly to REVIEWER (SECURITY-REVIEWER not required).
result.next_action: REVIEWER: confirm the deleted assertion was genuinely redundant (not load-bearing) and that no idiom/scope-creep concerns apply to a test-only deletion+rename. On PASS, route to TEST-DESIGNER per WF-03 (or directly to closeout if WF-03's issue-fix path treats this as already-covered-by-existing-tests). docs/issues/ISS-0469.yaml status update is DOC-UPDATER's normal closeout step once REVIEWER and TEST-RUNNER (if invoked) both PASS.
